title: Resisting Temptation
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Resisting temptation means standing against the pull toward sin by relying on God’s truth, grace, watchfulness, and help. Temptation is real, but God provides a way to endure and obey.
summary: Resisting temptation means standing against the pull toward sin by relying on God’s truth, grace, watchfulness, and help. Temptation is real, but God provides a way to endure and obey.
christFocus: Jesus Christ was tempted yet without sin, and He helps those who are tempted. His victory gives believers both a pattern of obedience and a merciful Savior to whom they can run for help.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Temptation is not sin by itself, but it is dangerous because it appeals to disordered desire. James teaches that desire can conceive and give birth to sin if it is entertained rather than resisted.

God does not abandon His people in temptation. He is faithful and provides a way of escape so believers may endure. This does not remove responsibility, but it gives hope that obedience is possible by grace.

Jesus resisted temptation with Scripture and faithful submission to the Father. Believers resist by watchfulness, prayer, truth, humility, and fleeing what feeds sin.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Temptation often feels private, powerful, and inevitable. People may believe they are uniquely trapped or that failure is unavoidable. Scripture says temptation is common, God is faithful, and help is available.

This doctrine strengthens believers in everyday warfare. The goal is not mere shame after failure, but active dependence before and during temptation.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Learn the patterns of your temptation and bring them into the light. Use Scripture, pray early, flee what feeds sin, seek wise accountability, and come boldly to Christ for mercy and help. Do not wait until desire has grown strong before resisting.
